newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P affirms TNT, off creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P affirms TNT, off creditwatch.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday it has affirmed the B-plus long term credit rating of TNT Ltd and has removed the rating from Creditwatch, where it was placed on November 20, 1995.

"The rating outlook is positive. Despite the Ansett sale, improving profitability and cash flow are prerequisites for a future rating improvement. Profitability is likely to improve gradually, given the recent restructuring efforts," S&P said.
On September 2, TNT entered into an agreement with Air New Zealand Ltd to sell 50 percent of Ansett Holdings Ltd for A$325 million.

S&P said existing ratings reflect TNT's leading market position in the global logistics and time-sensitive businesses, offset by highly competitive industry conditions and relatively poor profitability measures.
Increased competition and competitive pricing in the Australian market has meant that the European operations are the backbone of the company's profits, S&P said.

"Uncertainies regarding the strength of the economic environment in Europe during the next couple of years are important consideration when assessing business prospects for TNT," the ratings agency said.
It said TNT's 50 percent owned international parcel express business GD Express Worldwide "remains a problem, and further restructuring is likely."
"Bringing GD Express back to sustainable levels of earnings will take some time and continue to have an unfavourable impact in the company's asset quality, despite recently reduced losses," S&P said.
S&P said of TNT's other associated companies, Ansett Worldwide Aviation Services continues to downsize its aircraft leasing portfolio in an effort to minimise risk.

It said funds from the Ansett sale are likely to reduce debt including operating leases to under A$1.00 billion. Net debt to capital, adjusted for operating leases and the Ansett deal, is likely to fall to 50 percent from 60 percent at year end 1996.
"Importantly, the (Ansett) transaction will allow the company to defer its onerous near-term debt maturities and improve financial flexibility," S&P said.
